headline: The booth quotes its dates the way the papers print them
lede: Papers, Please-Min's deny strip used to cite serial numbers (1982.10.31) that no surface in the booth actually prints. Now every evidence line speaks the papers' own month-name shape — and the fairness contract was re-pinned to make serials illegal at the booth.

notes.text: The never-dry rung named the target: with slot a busy on its warden target, idle-kick scored PAPERS, PLEASE-MIN the weakest game on the shelf (score 5) and the session shipped its oldest honest gap — #1891's month-numerals tail.

EXPIRED, IDREQ and CURFEW evidence now print `OCT 31 1982 < TODAY NOV 01 1982`; paperscheck bans serials in evidence, demands every cited date be printed at the booth, and adds a no-clip corridor law — the old 2-line pin quietly passed clipped quotes.
One re-pin found a latent looseness: the wall-clock crowd law had measured the pre-#1891 serial header row for twelve sessions. Now it measures the 19-char month-name line reality prints.
23,406 checks with mutants (two new serial-revert mutants die), 134 live browser gates with real keys, prod chunk verified by tracing the minified date function.
